title: What is frequency capping | AppsFlyer mobile glossary

facts.fact: Frequency capping is an online advertising technique that limits the number of times an ad is shown to the same user to prevent fatigue.
facts.quote: Frequency capping is an online advertising technique that limits the number of times an ad is shown to the same user to prevent fatigue.

facts.fact: AppsFlyer identifies three elements to consider when setting frequency caps: frequency, creative, and timeframe.
facts.quote: There are three elements to consider when setting caps:

facts.fact: Ad platforms track how often a user sees an ad using unique identifiers such as cookies, device IDs, or tracking pixels, and check the cap before serving the ad.
facts.quote: Ad platforms track how often an ad or campaign is shown to the same users using unique identifiers like cookies, device IDs, or tracking pixels.

facts.fact: According to AppsFlyer, the impression is logged within milliseconds of the ad being served when the frequency cap has not been reached.
facts.quote: the impression is logged within milliseconds to maintain a seamless user experience.

facts.fact: AppsFlyer says mobile measurement partners use probabilistic modeling as a fallback when unique IDs are unavailable.
facts.quote: Mobile measurement partners (like AppsFlyer) effectively use probabilistic modeling as a fallback method when unique IDs are unavailable

facts.fact: AppsFlyer, citing Meta's research, says lower frequency is ideal for established brands with high market share, long purchase cycles, unique messages, and multiple media channels, while higher frequency suits new brands with low market share and short purchase cycles.
facts.quote: Ideal for established brands with high market share, long purchase cycles, unique messages, and multiple media channels.
